first_impression.reaction: Okay good, the very first lines actually answer me: remind before the date, follow up after, last call if someone's still blank. No pop-up, no life story. I'm on the train so I skimmed the takeaways and jumped straight to the text message wording, which is what I really came for.

journey.quote: Send a gentle reminder before your reply date, a personal follow-up once it has passed, and a last call only if a name is still blank.
journey.reaction: That's the answer in one sentence. Exactly what I wanted from Google.

journey.quote: Time every reminder from your own reply date and the date your venue and caterer need final numbers, not from a fixed rule.
journey.reaction: Fair, but part of me still wants 'just tell me how many weeks'. I get why it doesn't, it's honest at least.

journey.quote: Keep one guest list so only the people who have not replied hear from you again.
journey.reaction: Useful, but the takeaways don't say how many reminders to send. I had to scroll to find the 'three steps at most' bit, and that's the thing I'd want in the summary.

journey.section: The number of reminders to send
journey.quote: Plan on three steps at most: a gentle reminder, a personal follow-up and a last call.
journey.reaction: Good, clear. The heading reads a bit oddly though, I'd never type 'the number of reminders to send'. 'How many' is what I'd search.

journey.section: Who to remind and how to reach them
journey.quote: As general information as at November 2026, not legal advice: the Privacy Act does not cover individuals acting in a personal capacity, and in some situations state or territory laws may also apply.
journey.reaction: I'm just trying to nudge my cousins. Legal talk about the Privacy Act is more than I need here and slows me down. The 'don't send a group text' advice before it was enough.

journey.section: Wedding RSVP reminder text message wording
journey.quote: [Guest name]! Quick nudge from the two of us: your RSVP is the last piece of our puzzle. Reply by [reply date] at [RSVP web address] and we will save you a seat (and a glass).
journey.reaction: Love this. Copy, paste, done. Three tones is really handy, I'd use the light one for friends and formal for my aunties.

journey.section: When the reply date has passed
journey.quote: Light: [Guest name], this is our very last nudge, we promise. Yes or no by [new date] and we are all set.
journey.reaction: This is the one I'll actually need in a few weeks. Bookmarking for that.

journey.quote: No. A kind, personal reminder helps guests who meant to reply and forgot. It becomes rude only when it is repeated too heavily or sent to a group.
journey.reaction: Short and straight. The FAQ answers the exact questions I had in my head.

unanswered_questions: Roughly how long before my reply date is 'comfortable time' for the first reminder? The page tells me to work it out from my own dates but gives no ballpark.
Is this advice current for 2026? Apart from the privacy note, there's no date on the page that tells me when it was last checked.

turn_offs_found.why: Feels heavy and off-topic for someone who just wants reminder wording. Mild, I just scrolled past.

turn_offs_found.quote: ## The number of reminders to send

would_share_with: My fiancé, so he can send the reminders to his side
My mum, for the phone call script

cta_reaction.quote: If your guest list spans several countries and a weekend of events, talk to Wedded Concierge about planning the celebration around it.
cta_reaction.why: I came for wording, not a planner. It's not pushy and doesn't block anything, so it doesn't bother me, but I'm not enquiring from this page. I might click the Wonderland Studio link or the RSVP wording guide since those answer my next question.
